canonical_statement: The study evaluated whether one institution’s UFH VTE protocol achieved and maintained therapeutic anti-Xa levels during the first 48 hours of therapy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The purpose of this study was to evaluate the ability of one facility’s UFH VTE protocol to achieve and maintain therapeutic anti-Xa levels within the first 48 h of therapy.

canonical_statement: The study was a single-center retrospective chart review at Avera McKennan Hospital and University Health Center using records from May 2016 through September 2020.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This was a single-center study that was conducted at Avera McKennan Hospital and University Health Center via retrospective chart review.

canonical_statement: Eligible patients were adults at least 18 years old treated on the institutional VTE heparin protocol for 48 consecutive hours with at least one anti-Xa level.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Patients 18 years and older who were initiated on the institution’s VTE heparin dosing protocol for a consecutive 48 h with at least one anti-Xa level were included in the study.

population.label: Eligible adult VTE patients
inclusion_criteria: Institutional VTE heparin protocol for 48 consecutive hours

canonical_statement: Key exclusions included unconfirmed VTE, superficial venous thrombosis, UFH initiation outside the hospital, specified coagulopathies, thrombolysis, and recent anticoagulant exposure before UFH initiation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Exclusion criteria included the following: lack of confirmed VTE on duplex ultrasound or chest imaging, superficial venous thrombosis, and initiation of heparin at an outside hospital.

population.label: Excluded patients
exclusion_criteria: Recent oral or parenteral anticoagulant exposure

canonical_statement: Of 8,376 patients with an active heparin infusion order, 8,171 were excluded and 205 met study inclusion criteria; 89 received bolus plus infusion and 116 received infusion only.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Patients Meeting Inclusion Criteria (N = 205)

population.label: Adults with confirmed DVT and/or PE treated with the institutional UFH VTE protocol for 48 consecutive hours

canonical_statement: The institutional protocol used an initial infusion rate of approximately 18 units/kg/h rounded to weight-banded rates from 900 to 1,600 units/h and an optional initial bolus approximating 80 units/kg, capped at 8,000 units.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The study institution uses a UFH dosing protocol which provides a weight-based initial rate of approximately 18 units/kg/h

canonical_statement: Providers could omit the initial UFH bolus based on patient factors such as bleeding risk, creating bolus-plus-infusion and infusion-only cohorts.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Providers have the option of omitting the initial bolus dose based on patient factors (e.g., risk of bleeding).

exposures.details: Provider-selected bolus versus no bolus

canonical_statement: The institution defined therapeutic anti-Xa as 0.3–0.7 units/mL; values below 0.3 were subtherapeutic and values above 0.7 were supratherapeutic.

outcome.definition: Subtherapeutic <0.3 units/mL; therapeutic 0.3–0.7 units/mL; supratherapeutic >0.7 units/mL

canonical_statement: Anti-Xa levels were obtained every 6 hours until two consecutive therapeutic levels were reached, after which monitoring changed to daily.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Anti-Xa levels are obtained every 6 h until two consecutive therapeutic anti-Xa levels are achieved, at which point anti-Xa levels are ordered daily.

canonical_statement: Bedside nurses adjusted UFH according to the anti-Xa protocol, with rate changes or holds reflexing a pharmacist verification order; pharmacists checked the adjustment and contacted the nurse if correction was needed.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A pharmacist then double-checks that the heparin drip was correctly adjusted based on the protocol.

canonical_statement: For subsequent titration, patients at or below 70 kg and those above 70 kg had different bolus and rate-increase rules when anti-Xa was below 0.3 units/mL; supratherapeutic anti-Xa above 1 unit/mL prompted a 1-hour hold and a 200-unit/h rate decrease in both groups.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Greater than 1                        No bolus                                    Hold infusion for 1 h, then decrease rate by 200 units/h

exposures.details: ≤70 kg: anti-Xa <0.1 bolus 4000 U +200 U/h; 0.1–0.29 bolus 2000 U +100 U/h. >70 kg: anti-Xa <0.1 bolus 6000 U +300 U/h; 0.1–0.29 bolus 3000 U +100 U/h. 0.3–0.7 no change; 0.71–1 decrease 100 U/h; >1 hold 1 h then decrease 200 U/h.

canonical_statement: UFH initiation was defined as the first documented administration of the heparin infusion, and anti-Xa values were grouped into 6-hour windows around nominal time points.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Anti-Xa values were grouped by 6-h time intervals after the initiation of UFH

canonical_statement: The primary endpoint was the number of patients with at least one therapeutic heparin anti-Xa level during the first 48 hours of UFH therapy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The primary end point was to determine the number of patients who achieved at least one therapeutic heparin anti-Xa level within the first 48 h of UFH infusion therapy.

concept.text: At least one therapeutic anti-Xa level

outcome.definition: At least one anti-Xa value within the institution’s therapeutic range during the first 48 hours of UFH

canonical_statement: Secondary outcomes included therapeutic anti-Xa prevalence at each 6-hour interval, time to first therapeutic level, in-hospital mortality, hospital length of stay, subtherapeutic and supratherapeutic anti-Xa occurrence, and patient factors associated with anti-Xa results.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Secondary outcomes included the percentage of therapeutic levels at each 6-h interval during the first 48 h of therapy, time to first therapeutic level, in-hospital mortality, and hospital length of stay.

outcome.definition: Therapeutic status over time, time to first therapeutic anti-Xa, mortality, length of stay, out-of-range anti-Xa, and patient-factor analyses

canonical_statement: The analysis used Student’s t-test or Wilcoxon rank-sum test for continuous-group comparisons as appropriate, Fisher’s exact test for categorical variables, a 5% significance threshold, and R version 3.6.3.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Fisher’s exact test was used. In all statistical tests, an effect was considered statistically significant if the p value of its corresponding statistical test was not greater than 5%.

canonical_statement: The authors identified the small, retrospective, single-institution design as a limitation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This study has several limitations including its small, retrospective design. Also, it was conducted in a single institution

canonical_statement: No a priori sample-size calculation was performed, creating risk of type II error.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A sample size calculation was not performed a priori which leads to a risk for type II error.

canonical_statement: Multiple individuals performed eligibility review and data collection, which could have introduced inconsistencies despite use of standardized flowsheets.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: there were multiple individuals including/excluding patients and collecting data which may have led to inconsistencies.

canonical_statement: The number of anti-Xa levels drawn decreased over time, and protocol compliance was not measured, limiting interpretation of longitudinal therapeutic control.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We also noticed the number of anti-Xa levels drawn decreased over time.

canonical_statement: About 30% of patients started UFH in the ICU, raising potential selection bias toward a more complex population with greater anti-Xa variability.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: With about 30% of the overall group starting heparin in the intensive care unit, there may have been a selection bias with more complicated patients being put on heparin over other anticoagulants.

canonical_statement: Uneven distribution of anti-Xa measurements across time windows could have distorted interpretation of interval-specific therapeutic rates.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: uneven distribution of levels among different time windows may lead to inaccurate interpretation of the results.

canonical_statement: The study primarily assessed monitoring-oriented endpoints rather than patient-oriented outcomes, limiting direct clinical decision-making value.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: patient-oriented outcomes need to be assessed to have a clearer picture of the efficacy of a dosing protocol as the monitoring-oriented end points of our study are less useful in clinical decision-making.

canonical_statement: The authors concluded that most patients achieved at least one therapeutic anti-Xa level within 48 hours, but fewer consistently maintained therapeutic levels.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: most patients were able to achieve at least one therapeutic anti-Xa level within the first 48 h of initiation. However, fewer patients were able to consistently maintain therapeutic anti-Xa levels within this timeframe.

canonical_statement: The authors called for studies of alternative UFH dosing strategies that evaluate both consistency of therapeutic anti-Xa attainment and patient-oriented outcomes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Further studies are warranted to determine whether there are dosing strategies that could yield more consistent achievement of therapeutic anti-Xa levels and whether alternative dosing strategies would affect patient-oriented outcomes.
